history.summary: Shrine of Konung Lairembi, the protector goddess of Bishnupur town in the Meitei Umang Lai tradition. It stands on the historic hillock at Tengkhal Khunou (also the site of C.I. College, Bishnupur), where, by local belief, the first Rasa Lila (Rasa dance) was performed. A Manipur temple guide locates it on CI College Road, Bishnupur (entry free, open sunrise to sunset). Unlike the town's well-documented Vishnu temple, the shrine's founding, dynasty and antiquity are not recorded in available sources - details UNVERIFIED.

name: Konung Lairembi Temple
town_description: Bishnupur is the headquarters town of Bishnupur district in the Manipur valley, about 30 km south of Imphal. It is known for its ancient temples, including the famous 15th-century Vishnu Temple, and is closely associated with the Moirang legend and Manipuri Vaishnavism. The town sits near Loktak Lake, the largest freshwater lake in Northeast India.

travel.railway: No railway station in the district; nearest railheads are Dimapur (Nagaland) and Silchar (Assam), 150+ km away (verify)
